hypotheses: At rho=0, guardrail selection (C) reduces metered traffic and wasted work; its final-window accuracy is similar to or better than random selection (A).
As rho increases, guardrail selection (C) becomes less representative of profile-linked classes; random over-selection (B) may improve coverage at higher resource cost.
Policy D's staleness bonus should reduce participation imbalance among eligible vehicles without violating guardrails.
Connectable peer pairs may show class-coverage bias when parked Wi-Fi availability correlates with usage profile.

metric_refresh.worst_class_accuracy_pct: Recomputed as min(per_class_accuracy_pct); removed erroneous extra factor of 100.
metric_refresh.participation_diagnostics: Participation minima, max-min spread, under-five counts, and selected-client-round-normalized resource metrics were recomputed from per-run records.
metric_refresh.participation_weighted_class_mix_pct: Recomputed from each seed's recorded client profiles, partition labels, and per-client participation counts.
metric_refresh.profile_assignment_note: Historical profile assignments are retained as recorded. The current simulator now uses seed-invariant client-ID assignments; this artifact predates that correction and reports profile_assignments_fixed_across_seeds=false.

staleness_bonus_diagnostic.description: Selection-only diagnostic; no model training or resource accounting.
